subject: Incident 3784: Elevated retry loops causing generation tail latency — initial bulletin and follow-ups
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: emily.park@crestwave.ai, jacob.torres@crestwave.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Incident 3784 — Elevated retry loops affecting generation tail (initial bulletin)

Hi Emily / Jacob,

We're reaching out with an operational bulletin: starting at 08:45 PT today our telemetry detected an increased frequency of client-side retries that amplified generation tail latency for hosted text-generation endpoints. You may observe higher-than-usual p95/p99 for longer sequences and intermittent timeouts for some requests.

What we know so far:
- Window observed: ~08:45–09:00 PT (investigation continuing).
- Root signal: a transient coordination regression between our rate-limiter and the retry gating logic that caused multiple backend retries for partially-completed streams.
- Impact: elevated p95/p99 and an increase in 502/504 for a subset of multi-chunk generation requests. Estimated affected traffic: ~3–5% of requests across us-west clusters.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Activated blue-green fallback for the affected routing tier to reduce retry amplification.
- Scoped a hotfix to the retry gating logic and deployed to a portion of the fleet at 09:05 PT.
- Enabled targeted throttling for heavy-sequence requests to maintain overall system stability.

What to expect next:
- We'll post a short status update to our status page (link below) within the next 20–30 minutes and follow with a resolution/update once the hotfix fully rolls out.
- If you see persistent errors or timeouts from your integration, please reply with example request IDs and timestamps — that will help us prioritize.

Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/3784
Ticket: INF-4921

Attachments: incident_summary_3784.pdf (summary), p95_latency_trend_20281102.png (early chart)

We're sorry for the disruption — we know these tail issues directly affect inference-dependent workflows. I'll follow up as soon as we have mitigation confirmation.

Thanks,
Olga
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Incident 3784 — Elevated retry loops affecting generation tail (initial bulletin)

Hi Jacob — thanks for the quick note and for offering request IDs; that would help.

Roll-forward ETA:
- Hotfix staged at 09:05 PT and progressively rolled across the routing tier. We expected traffic normalization by ~09:30–09:45 PT for most customers. During rollout we observed a subset of flows that still experienced elevated tail latency due to cached retry tokens that persisted briefly.

Recommended immediate mitigations on your side:
- If possible, temporarily relax your client retry policy for long-running generation requests: increase the backoff multiplier and lower the max retry attempts to avoid amplifying transient backend retries.
- If you have per-request timeout control, increasing the timeout window by ~5–10s for multi-chunk jobs reduces false client-side timeouts during the tail correction period.

We've attached a short summary and a p95 chart. We're continuing to monitor — Marissa is running the mitigation playbook and Aditya is owning the rollback/verification steps. Ben is standing by for account questions if you need SLA/credits guidance.

If you can share 2–3 sample request IDs from the 08:50–09:10 window, we'll pull traces and confirm whether those hit the retry amplification path.

Regards,
Olga

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: emily.park@crestwave.ai, jacob.torres@crestwave.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Nov 2028 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Incident 3784 — final update and postmortem link (resolved)

Hello Emily / Jacob,

Final update: the incident has been resolved and services returned to expected baselines by 11/02 10:45 PT after a controlled rollout of the retry-gating hotfix and cache invalidation of retry tokens.

Root cause (summary):
- A mismatched invariants change in the routing layer rate-limiter caused duplicate retry triggers for partially-completed streams when combined with our client-side retry heuristics.
- The combination produced amplification on long-sequence generations, increasing p95/p99 and producing transient 502/504 errors.

Remediation completed:
- Hotfix to the gating logic deployed and validated across the fleet.
- Automated rollback hooks and additional unit tests added to prevent the invariant mismatch.
- A short-term telemetry rule added to detect retry amplification patterns for earlier alerting.

What you can read now:
- Incident postmortem (public summary): https://drive.redwood.com/incident/3784/postmortem
- Status page incident: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/3784
- Internal ticket (for reference): INF-4921

Credits/SLA: Ben will follow up separately if you want us to evaluate an account credit for the window of elevated errors.

We appreciate your patience and the quick signal you provided; your request IDs helped us trace the amplification path faster. If you'd like a short review call to walk through the postmortem and changes we made, I'm happy to schedule one.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
